note: Description taken from Holmgren's 1910 original description of Eutermes bivalens (in German), including two soldier size classes and the worker; alate unknown. Type localities Coxipó/Cuyabá, Mato Grosso, Brazil, and Estancia Postillon, Paraguay. Holmgren refers the 'two size classes of soldiers' recorded by Silvestri 1903 as E. Rippertii to this species. The worker body length figure is incomplete in the OCR and is not cited. The original is in German and the BHL scan OCR is only moderate: decimal points are often misread as commas or colons and some measurement digits are blurred; blurred values are not cited. The species was then placed in Eutermes and is now in Nasutitermes.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier includes two distinct size classes (major soldier body length 4.5—5 mm, head length 1.4—1.45 mm; minor soldier body length 3—4 mm, head length 1.2—1.35 mm); the head capsule profiles of the two differ: in the major soldier the frons is distinctly concave and the vertex forms a distinct angle with the nasus, while in the minor soldier the vertex and nasus lie in the same plane and only the base of the nasus is slightly elevated. Holmgren considers this species to be the 'two size classes of soldiers' form that Silvestri recorded as E. Rippertii.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Major soldier: head capsule dark brown, nasus tip paler; antennae and legs pale rusty brown, anterior margin of the pronotum brown, nota and sternites pale rusty brown. Head with only a few bristles at the base of the nasus and on the vertex; abdominal tergites smooth, with only a marginal bristle row; sternites with short hairs and marginal bristles. Head broadly oval, nasus conical; frontal outline distinctly concave, the vertex forming a distinct angle with the nasus. Antennae 14-segmented: segment 2 equal to segment 3, segment 4 very slightly shorter. Pronotum strongly saddle-shaped, the anterior margin upturned at almost a right angle to the posterior lobe and not concave. Measurements: body length 4.5—5 mm; head length 1.4—1.45 mm (the modal class also falls here); head width 0.80—0.95 mm (modal class 0.90—0.95 mm). Minor soldier: colour and pilosity as in the major soldier; head oval, nasus conical, vertex and nasus in the same plane, the base of the nasus with a weak elevation; antennae 12 or 13-segmented. Measurements: body length 3—4 mm; head length 1.2—1.35 mm (modal class 1.20—1.25 mm); head width 0.70—0.75 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head brown, the head capsule sutures, genae, anterior margin of the transverse band, antennal basal spots, antennae and mandible bases dirty yellow. Cephalic bristles rather sparse; abdominal plates with short hairs, the marginal bristle row of the tergites not very distinct, sternite bristles thicker. Head broad, quadrangular-oval, slightly wider anteriorly; postclypeus rather arched, shorter than half its width, touching the large bare mandibular process. Antennae rather short, 14-segmented: segment 2 equal to the sum of the next two, segment 5 slightly longer than segment 4. Pronotum saddle-shaped, upturned at an obtuse angle, anterior margin very weakly concave.
